Subject: QBR flight deck: sales readiness + account profiles

Team —

We’re on the hook for the QBR sales slot on May 22. I want a compact, operational deck that the GTM leadership can use to call out runway, ask-softs, and where we need cross-functional pressure. Please treat this as the single source for exec review: a one-slide account profile per top 12 accounts + a consolidated forecast slide.

Asks (please):
- Use the attached QBR_Account_Template.xlsx. One row per customer, 6 bullets max (deal status, ARR impact, close window, blockers, key ask, recommended action).
- Update your forecast column (best/likely/worst) in the rollup tab — we'll use the consolidated numbers in the deck.
- Flag any accounts needing leadership engagement (support ask + why). Put *LEAD* in the "Escalation" column.

Deadlines:
- Template updates by EOD Thu, May 13.
- Final deck review Mon, May 17 (I’ll circulate v3 for sign-off).

Attach: QBR_Account_Template.xlsx (stub) — use it as the canonical source. I’ll consolidate into QBR_FlightDeck_v3.pptx and run a prep with execs on the 20th.

Quick note on style: keep each account profile vendor-agnostic; call out technical dependencies (SE work) and procurement blockers separately.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov | Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Olga —

Uploading my completed rows and a short account-by-account note below (also added to the spreadsheet). Quick hits for the top 5 in my book:

1) Acme Cloud (deal_id: ACME-1129) — Likely close: June. ARR: $420k/Y. Risk: procurement legal redline on data residency (they need examples of on-prem private offerings). Ask: SE onsite demo + security brief. *LEAD* 

2) Nimbus Health (NIM-703) — Best: May close, Likely: Q3. ARR: $270k/Y. Risk: integration with their legacy ETL. Ask: assign SWEng for connector scoping + product checkpoint.

3) GigaRetail (GIGA-451) — Procurement paused pending consolidated PO. ARR: $180k/Y. Risk: budget approval timing (retail seasonality). Ask: Offer 60-day payment terms + procurement contact intro.

4) Orion Labs — Small proof-of-value, upsell pipeline into dedicated. ARR: $95k/Y. Healthy, low-risk.

5) TerraFine — Stalled; legal returned redlines to SOW. ARR: $55k/Y. Needs legal backlog prioritized.

Attachment: I attached QBR_FlightDeck_v2.pptx (deck with my slides). I didn’t merge forecasts — left that to Rishi.

- Marissa
Senior Account Executive

Thanks — I pulled Marissa's rows and rolled my book into the forecast_rollup_20270514.csv (attached). A few notes on consolidation approach so leadership has clarity:

- Rollup logic: We use Likely as our ops-facing single-point forecast. Best/Worst columns preserved for scenario modelling in the appendix.
- Adjustment: For accounts flagged *LEAD*, I applied a -15% probability dampener to Likely until we confirm leadership action/commitments.
- Regional split: US / EU / APAC tags are in column F. I flagged Acme Cloud as "US", Nimbus Health as "US".

High-risk flags I added: Acme Cloud (data residency/legal), GigaRetail (procurement cadence), TerraFine (legal redlines). See column "Risk Note".

Attachment: forecast_rollup_20270514.csv (stub)

Questions for the group:
- For *LEAD* accounts, do we want an explicit "support ask" slide per account (1 slide each) or consolidate them into a single escalation slide? My recommendation: single escalation slide with a callout box per account — easier for exec time.

Thoughts?

-Rishi
Director, Sales Operations
